study_design: Prospective cohort analysis in the Cancer Prevention Study II Nutrition Cohort, with race-specific analyses among Black and White men.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: After excluding men with a history of cancer and incomplete dietary information, 692 Black and 64,856 White men were included in the cohort.
reason: The abstract evaluates incident prostate cancer overall and does not report an aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint. The total participant and case counts are sums of the explicitly reported Black and White subgroup counts.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Among Black men, total red meat intake (processed plus unprocessed red meat) was associated with higher risk of prostate cancer (RR, 2.0; 95% CI, 1.0-4.2 for highest versus lowest quartile; P(trend) = 0.05); this increase in risk was mainly due to risk associated with consumption of cooked processed meats (sausages, bacon, and hot dogs; RR, 2.7; 95% CI, 1.3-5.3 for highest versus lowest quartile; P(trend) = 0.008).
estimate_classifications.reason: The cooked processed-meat estimate is for incident prostate cancer overall among Black men.
